name: Synology DSM
description: Synology DiskStation Manager: system and storage health, shared folders, running tasks, Download Station queue and the file station tree. Session-login auth against your own NAS.
instructions:
**Setup**
1. In DSM create a user for the integration. Give it read access to the shared folders the agent should see and, if you want the system tools, membership of the administrators group — several `SYNO.Core` endpoints are admin-only.
2. **Turn off two-factor authentication for that user**, or the login call cannot complete. This is the main reason to use a dedicated account rather than your own.
3. Set `SYNOLOGY_URL` to your NAS (e.g. `https://nas.example.com:5001`, no trailing slash), plus `SYNOLOGY_USERNAME` and `SYNOLOGY_PASSWORD`.

**DSM's session is a `sid`.** The adapter logs in at `/webapi/auth.cgi` and passes the returned `sid` back as a cookie on every call, re-logging in when DSM expires it. AnythingMCP keeps the session encrypted in `connector_auth_cache`.

**Every call names an API, a version and a method.** DSM's Web API is one CGI endpoint per family with `api`, `version` and `method` as query parameters — `entry.cgi?api=SYNO.Core.System&version=1&method=info`. That is why the tools here look repetitive in the trace; the parameters are what distinguish them.

**Success is in the body, not the status code.** DSM answers `{"success": false, "error": {"code": 105}}` with HTTP 200. Code 105 is 'insufficient permission', 119 'session expired', 400 'no such account or wrong password'. A 200 is not a result.

**Valid TLS is required, and a fresh DSM does not have it.** Synology ships a self-signed certificate; this connector will refuse it. DSM has built-in Let's Encrypt support under **Control Panel → Security → Certificate** — use it.

**Read-only by design**: no file writes, no share changes, no package management.

**Self-hosted, which is the thing to plan for.**
- On **AnythingMCP Cloud** the instance must be reachable from the public internet on a real hostname with a valid TLS certificate. A self-signed certificate will fail: the connector offers no trust-anything switch, and a homelab's default certificate is exactly the case that breaks.
- On an internal host (`nas.intern`, `10.0.0.x`), self-host AnythingMCP on the same network and add that host to `SSRF_ALLOWED_HOSTS`, or the outbound guard refuses the call before it is made.

tools.name: synology_list_apis
tools.description: List the Web APIs this DSM publishes, with the version range and CGI path of each. Start here — DSM versions differ in what they expose, and this is the authority.

tools.name: synology_get_system_info
tools.description: Read the NAS's system information: model, serial number, DSM version, uptime, CPU and total memory.

tools.name: synology_get_system_utilization
tools.description: Read live utilisation: CPU load, memory in use, disk throughput and network throughput right now.

tools.name: synology_list_storage
tools.description: Read the storage overview: every volume and disk with its size, used space, filesystem and SMART health status. Where a failing disk shows up.

tools.name: synology_list_shares
tools.description: List the shared folders with their name, path, description and whether each is encrypted — the map of what is on the NAS.

tools.name: synology_list_files
tools.description: List the files and folders under one path in File Station, with their size, type and modification time.

sort_by.description: Sort field: name, size, user, group, mtime, atime, ctime or type.

tools.name: synology_search_files
tools.description: Start a File Station search under one path for a filename pattern. Returns a task id — DSM's search is asynchronous by design.

folder_path.description: Absolute DSM path to search under, e.g. /volume1.

tools.name: synology_list_download_tasks
tools.description: List the Download Station queue with each task's title, status, size, progress and speed — what the NAS is currently fetching.

tools.name: synology_list_users
tools.description: List the DSM user accounts with their name, description, e-mail and whether each is expired or disabled. Requires an administrator account.
